```{r}
library(sp)
library(maps)
library(sf)
library(lattice)
library(tidyverse)
library(geoR)
library(gstat)
library(INLA)
```


Loading data

```{r}
data(meuse)
data(meuse.grid)
```


Model to build:

$$Y(s) = X(s)'\beta + \epsilon(s)$$
$$\epsilon(s) \sim \textrm{Gaussian Process}$$ 
Spatial Covariance Structures to consider:

Exponential: 
$$\textrm{Cov}\{\epsilon(s), \epsilon(s+h)\} = \sigma^2 e^{- |h / \phi|} $$

Gaussian:

$$\textrm{Cov}\{\epsilon(s), \epsilon(s+h)\} = \sigma^2 exp{- |h / \phi |^2}$$

Spherical:
$$
\textrm{Cov}\{\epsilon(s), \epsilon(s+h)\} = 
\begin{cases}
  \sigma^2(1-\frac{3}{2}|h/ \phi| + \frac{1}{2}|h / \phi|^3) & \text{if } h \leq \phi, \\
  0 & \text{if } h > \phi
\end{cases}
$$


# Data visualization

```{r}
# configuring meuse dataset
coordinates(meuse) <- ~ x + y
proj4string(meuse) <- CRS("epsg:28992")

# configure meuse grid dataset (has distance from meuse river pre-calculated for each location)
data(meuse.grid)
coordinates(meuse.grid) <- ~ x + y
proj4string(meuse.grid) <- CRS("epsg:28992")
gridded(meuse.grid) <- TRUE
```


```{r}
meuse.grid.poly <- as(meuse.grid, "SpatialPolygons") # making meuse.grid belong to the SpatialPolygons class
meuse.bdy <- surveillance::unionSpatialPolygons(meuse.grid.poly)
plot(meuse.bdy)
plot(meuse, add = TRUE, pch = 1)
```

```{r}
# plotting distance to river
spplot(meuse, "dist.m", do.log = FALSE, colorkey = TRUE)

# plotting lead concentration
spplot(meuse, "lead", do.log = TRUE, colorkey = FALSE)

bubble(meuse, "lead", do.log = TRUE, key.space = "bottom")
```

Clearly lead concentration is higher near the river. What will that graph look like when we remove the main effect of distance to river?

```{r}
lead.lm <- lm(log(lead) ~ sqrt(dist), data = meuse)
summary(lead.lm) # dist to river is significant as expected

meuse$fitted.lead = predict(lead.lm, data = meuse)
meuse$fitted.lead = meuse$fitted.lead - mean(meuse$fitted.lead)

meuse$resid.lead = residuals(lead.lm)

spplot(meuse, c("fitted.lead", "resid.lead"))
```

After removing the main effect of distance to river, there is still some inherent spatial pattern occuring in the residuals...

Since these residuals are clearly not independent, we must take a different modeling approach and include a spatial random effect in our model to account for these 


# Empirical Variogram

Empirical variograms are helpful for setting priors.

Based on the graph below, we'd want to set a penalizing complexity (PC) prior on sigma2 as Pr(sigma2 > 0.3) = 0.05 and a PC prior on phi of Pr(phi < 500) = 0.05. These are both subjective but seem to be appropriate for the data we have.

```{r}
meuse_geodat <- as.geodata(
  data.frame(
    coords = coordinates(meuse),
    data = resid(lead.lm)
  )
)

empirical_variog <- variog(meuse_geodat, max.dist = 1500, estimator.type = 'classical')

plot(empirical_variog, main = "Semivariogram")

# checking for presence of anisotropy 
#plot(variogram(lead ~ dist, data=meuse, alpha=c(0,45,90,135)))  # looks good enough
```



# Kriging


INLA (Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation) will be used to fit a bayesian prediction surface to our data. 


```{r}
# getting our meuse boundary
meuse.grid.poly <- as(meuse.grid, "SpatialPolygons")
meuse.boundary <- surveillance::unionSpatialPolygons(meuse.grid.poly)
plot(meuse.boundary)

# adding a mesh over this region
boundary.pts <- meuse.boundary@polygons[[1]]@Polygons[[1]]@coords # getting coords of boundary points
mesh <- fmesher::fm_mesh_2d_inla(loc = meuse@coords,
                                 loc.domain = boundary.pts, 
                                 max.edge = c(150, 500), # 150 length of triangles inside boundary, 500 length outside boundary
                                 offset = c(100, 250)) # 100 inner extension of mesh around meuse boundary, 250 outer extension

# plotting mesh and adding the meuse boundary and observation points
plot(mesh)
plot(meuse.boundary, add = TRUE, col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.25), lwd = 2) # meuse boundary
points(meuse@coords, pch = 16, col = rgb(1,0,0,0.2), cex = 0.9) # observation points
```


# Prior sensitivity tests
```{r}
######## Sensitivity of range prior #######

# Short-range prior  
spde_short_range <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  alpha = 2, # nu = 1
  prior.range = c(500, 0.05), # P(phi < 500m) = 0.05
  prior.sigma = c(0.5, 0.05) # P(sigma > 0.5) = 0.05
)

# Medium-range prior
spde_medium_range <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  alpha = 2,
  prior.range = c(1000, 0.05), # P(phi < 1000m) = 0.05
  prior.sigma = c(0.5, 0.05)
)

# Long-range prior
spde_long_range <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  alpha = 2,
  prior.range = c(2000, 0.05), # P(phi < 2000m) = 0.05 
  prior.sigma = c(0.5, 0.05)
)


######### Sensitivity of sigma (partial sill) priors ###########

spde_small_sigma <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  alpha = 2, # nu = 1
  prior.range = c(1000, 0.05), # P(phi < 500m) = 0.05
  prior.sigma = c(0.1, 0.05) # P(sigma > 0.1) = 0.05
)

spde_medium_sigma <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  alpha = 2, # nu = 1
  prior.range = c(1000, 0.05), # P(phi < 500m) = 0.05
  prior.sigma = c(0.5, 0.05) # P(sigma > 0.5) = 0.05
)

spde_large_sigma <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  alpha = 2, # nu = 1
  prior.range = c(1000, 0.05), # P(phi < 500m) = 0.05
  prior.sigma = c(1, 0.05) # P(sigma > 1) = 0.05
)



####### INLA structural setup

meuse$loglead <- log(meuse$lead) # making output variable explicit in dataframe

# Observation matrix (maps spatial field to our observed locations)
A_matrix <- inla.spde.make.A( # 155 x n_mesh matrix
  mesh = mesh,
  loc = coordinates(meuse)
)

# Prediction matrix (maps spatial field to grid of locations in the study area)
A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A( # n_grid x n_mesh matrix
  mesh = mesh,
  loc = coordinates(meuse.grid)
)

# Spatial index (tells INLA how to organize the latent spatial random effects)
s.index <- inla.spde.make.index(
  name = "spatial.field",
  n.spde = spde_short_range$n.spde
)

# Model stack (organizes all the model parts properly for INLA)
stack.modelfit <- inla.stack(
  data = list(loglead = meuse$loglead),
  A = list(A_matrix, 1),
  effects = list(
    s.index,
    data.frame(
      Intercept = 1,
      dist = meuse$dist
    )
  ),
  tag = "data"
)

# Prediction stack
stack.pred <- inla.stack(
  data = list(loglead = NA), # we don't know lead concentrations at predicted locations!
  A = list(A.pred, 1),
  effects = list(
    s.index,
    data.frame(
      Intercept = 1,
      dist = meuse.grid$dist
    )
  ),
  tag = "pred"
)

# combining the model and prediction stacks
join.stack <- inla.stack(stack.modelfit, stack.pred)


# function that fits the same model under whichever SPDE prior we provide
fit_spatial_model <- function(spde) {

  inla(
    loglead ~ -1 + Intercept + dist +
      f(spatial.field, model = spde),

    data = inla.stack.data(join.stack),

    control.predictor = list(
      A = inla.stack.A(join.stack),
      compute = TRUE
    ),

    control.compute = list(
      cpo = TRUE,
      dic = TRUE
    ),

    family = "gaussian"
  )
}

fit_short_range <- fit_spatial_model(spde_short_range)
fit_medium_range <- fit_spatial_model(spde_medium_range)
fit_long_range <- fit_spatial_model(spde_long_range)

fit_small_sigma <- fit_spatial_model(spde_small_sigma)
fit_medium_sigma <- fit_spatial_model(spde_medium_sigma)
fit_large_sigma <- fit_spatial_model(spde_large_sigma)

summary(fit_short_range)
summary(fit_medium_range)
summary(fit_long_range)


# prior sensitivity for sigma

# fixed effects
fit_small_sigma$summary.fixed
fit_medium_sigma$summary.fixed
fit_large_sigma$summary.fixed


# prior sensitivity for range

# fixed effects
fit_short_range$summary.fixed
fit_medium_range$summary.fixed
fit_long_range$summary.fixed

# hyperparams
# Range sensitivity
fit_short_range$summary.hyperpar
fit_medium_range$summary.hyperpar
fit_long_range$summary.hyperpar

# Sigma sensitivity
fit_small_sigma$summary.hyperpar
fit_medium_sigma$summary.hyperpar
fit_large_sigma$summary.hyperpar


### MAKE SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS SUMMARY TABLE HERE ###
```



The sensitivity test for varying priors of sigma and the range (phi) show that the choice of prior has minimal effects on the model results for the fixed effects.



# Choosing sensible choices for sigma, phi priors

Based on the empirical variogram earlier, good prior dist choices are penalizing complexity (PC) prior on sigma2 as Pr(sigma2 > 0.3) = 0.05 and a PC prior on phi of Pr(phi < 500) = 0.05.

We are looking at sigma, so a prior should be set on sigma as $Pr(\sigma > \sqrt{0.3}) = 0.05$.

```{r}
spde_final_model <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  alpha = 2, # nu = 1
  prior.range = c(500, 0.05), # P(phi < 500m) = 0.05
  prior.sigma = c(sqrt(0.3), 0.05) # P(sigma > sqrt(0.3)) = 0.05
)

fit_final_model <- fit_spatial_model(spde_final_model)

fit_final_model$summary.fixed
fit_final_model$summary.random
```



The posterior mean for distance is -2.26, and it appears to have a meaningfully strong relationship with the log(lead) concentration. Thus, for each one meter increase in distance, the log(lead) concentration decreases by 2.26 units.
